title: Your agent has entered the terminal
summary: Live flight tracking for your AI agents, with 100,000+ flights a day, delays and cancellations at 3,900+ airports, plus ground stops and security lines.
body_markdown:
Airports have always run on agents. There's the gate agent who knows your flight is delayed about ten minutes before the board does. There's the ticket agent who can somehow rebook you through Charlotte. And there's the travel agent, who back in the day handled all of it while you got on with your life.


Most of us lost that last one a while ago. Now it's coming back, with fewer brochures.


Introducing live flight tracking for your AI agents. With the Firecrawl plugin, your agent can now do three things.


- **Track 100,000+ flights a day,** live.
- **Check delays and cancellations** at 3,900+ airports.
- **See ground stops and security lines** right now, not as of whenever someone last updated a status page.


That's the feature. If you're already in the car,[skip to the gate](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/go/flights) . Otherwise, stick around through boarding.


## Missed connections


It's holiday travel season. You've got the airline app open in one tab, a flight tracker in another, and a third site that's meant to tell you whether the TSA line is "a little busy" or "bring a sandwich" busy. None of them talk to each other.


That's the real problem with travel data. It isn't secret. It just has bad connections. Your flight status lives in one place, delays at your departure airport in another, ground stops somewhere else again, and the security line is mostly guesswork.


Agents are good at exactly this. They check lots of places at once, put the answers together and tell you the one thing you care about. Leave now. Or relax, you're delayed 90 minutes. Go get a pretzel. What they've been missing is a reliable connection to live data. Live flight tracking is that connection.


## Ask it like a gate agent


Ask your agent the way you'd ask a gate agent.


> "Is my 6:40 flight out of Denver tonight on time? And how bad is security there right now?"


> "I've got a 45-minute connection in Atlanta. Are there any ground stops I should know about?"


> "My mom lands at O'Hare around 3. Tell me if that changes."


Your agent works out which flights and airports you mean, pulls live status and answers in plain language. There's no waiting for an announcement over a speaker that sounds like it's underwater.


It works as well in an actual terminal as an airport one. If you're building your own travel agent (the software kind), you get the same live data from your own harness.


## Why we built it this way


Flight status, airport delays and security lines live in different places and change by the minute. Alexandria brings them together, so your agent makes one call and gets current answers back.


That's how we think about Alexandria in general. Your agent should spend its time helping you, not hunting for the data.


## Check-in


1. Install the Firecrawl plugin in your agent and sign in to a Firecrawl account on a team where Alexandria is enabled.
2. Ask about a flight or an airport.
3. Go pack. We both know you haven't.


Everything's at[alexandria.firecrawl.dev/go/flights](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/go/flights) .


## Before you board


- Your agent can tell you a flight is delayed. It can't make the weather in Chicago clear up, and honestly neither can the gate agent, no matter how nicely you ask.
- If there's an airport or data point you want that isn't here yet, tell us. A lot of what's in Alexandria is there because someone asked for it.


Safe travels, smooth connections, and may your gate be on the same concourse.
